headerTitle: Wonder Woman • mamahtâw iskwew • ᒪᒪᐦᑖᐤ ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ

photo.alt: Wonder Woman trail sign showing a black female-warrior silhouette with hair, star tiara, and lariat, with red Plains Cree syllabics across the torso
photo.caption: 3D printed plaque: black Wonder-Woman silhouette with star tiara and lariat, the syllabics ᒪᒪᐦᑖᐤ ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ in red across the body.

morphemes.gloss: VII / pre-noun: ‘s/he or it is wondrous, miraculous, supernatural, possessing extraordinary power.’ Functions adjectivally before the noun (cf. mamahtâwisiw ‘s/he is wondrous, has spirit-power’).
NA noun (animate): ‘woman, female adult human.’ The everyday word for woman, distinct from nâpêw ‘man.’

relatedForms.english: S/he is wondrous / has spirit-power (the AI verb)

morphemes.gloss: AI verb final, 3sg independent: ‘s/he is in such-and-such a state’

relatedForms.note: The most common AI verb form. Used to describe people who possess remarkable abilities, especially spiritual/healing power.
VII parallel form: ‘it is wondrous.’ The plaque uses the bare prefixal mamahtâw before iskwew.
Plural form (‘wonder-women / wondrous women’). The pre-noun mamahtâw does not inflect.

quickReference.note: Headword on the plaque. Pre-noun mamahtâw + NA iskwew.
AI verb form. Often used of people with remarkable healing or spiritual powers.
Nominalised: ‘miraculousness, spirit-power, ability to do wondrous things.’

culturalStory.heading: About mamahtâw iskwew — the Wondrous Woman
body: The mamahtâw iskwew plaque turns the comic-book Wonder Woman into a nehiyaw (Plains Cree) figure. The black silhouette is unmistakable — the star tiara, the wave of hair, the lariat looped around both arms — but the syllabics across the torso, ᒪᒪᐦᑖᐤ ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ, render the name in a register the Amazonian original never had: mamahtâw is the same word the language uses for spirit-power, for healers, for people who do remarkable things. ‘Wondrous woman’ is the literal gloss; ‘miracle woman’ is closer to the cultural feel.

The phrase is a pre-noun + noun construction. mamahtâw is a VII (it-is-wondrous) used adjectivally before the noun: it does not inflect. iskwew is the everyday NA noun for ‘woman.’ The same root surfaces in the AI verb mamahtâwisiw ‘s/he has spirit-power, s/he does wondrous things,’ and in the abstract noun mamahtâwisiwin ‘miraculousness, spirit-power.’ The naming choice is deliberate: it lifts a pop-culture superhero into a category — the wondrous one, the one with spirit-power — that already exists in nehiyawêwin and that names actual people in Cree communities.

The trail itself is a 327 m stretch in the Hawrelak network on the south side of the river, in the same cluster as Lovers Lane, Victoria’s Secret, Purple Haze, and Back Breaker — short, blue-difficulty, tucked behind Government House and the Korean Pavilion. Trailforks itself lists the AKA mamahtâw iskwew for the trail. The land is ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory). The plaque’s red syllabics on a black silhouette pop against the bare white background — language and image carrying the same idea in two scripts.

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE: The plaque is carved with SRO 'mamahtâw iskwew' (with circumflex on the â). The current catalogue creeName 'mamahtaw iskwew' is missing the â circumflex. Trailforks's AKA listing for trail #31377 also writes 'mamahtâw iskwew' (with â). Coordinator should update catalogue creeName to 'mamahtâw iskwew'.

PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE (syllabics): The carved syllabics shows the long-â glyph ᑖ (with dot above) in the fourth position of mamahtâw — i.e. 'ᒪᒪᐦᑖᐤ.' The current catalogue creeSyllabics 'ᒪᒪᐦᑕᐤ ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ' has plain ᑕ (short a) in that position. Coordinator should update creeSyllabics to ᒪᒪᐦᑖᐤ ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ.

Note the legacy folder name 'mamahtaw_askwew' contains a typo ('askwew' for 'iskwew'). The folder is not renamed (per coordinator instructions); the catalogue 'folder' field correctly points to the existing path. The PAGE displays the corrected 'iskwew' / ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ in all carved-text positions.

iskwew syllabics: the carved plaque uses the decomposed form 'ᐃᐢᑲᐧᐤ' (i + s + ka + w-medial + w-final). The unified-syllabic form 'ᐃᐢᑵᐤ' (i + s + kwê + w) is also valid and is what itwêwina uses. The page uses the carved decomposed form for fidelity to the plaque, but the related-forms section uses the unified form for the plural ᐃᐢᑵᐘᐠ where it reads more naturally.

Morpheme analysis treats mamahtâw as an indeclinable pre-noun (the VII bare stem used adjectivally) plus the NA noun iskwew. An alternative analysis writes it as a single compound 'mamahtâwiskwew' meaning ‘wondrous-woman’ (single word). Both readings are linguistically defensible; the two-word reading is preferred here because the plaque visually separates the words and Trailforks’s AKA also separates them.

Trailforks pick: 'Wonder Woman' (trail id 31377), Hawrelak / NW Edmonton — 327m blue singletrack with a black-diamond climb, behind Government House. Trailhead 53.54092, -113.54308. High confidence (Trailforks lists AKA ‘mamahtâw iskwew’).
